key_insight: lPINN freezes a pretrained nonlinear neural basis offline and solves new PDE instances online with only a linear layer, combining reduced-order efficiency with physics-informed accuracy.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster forward and inverse simulation for differential equations while preserving differentiable, mesh-transferable solutions useful in scientific computing workflows.
method: Pretrain continuous neural basis functions on an ensemble of solution data with derivatives or physics residuals.
Freeze the hidden layers and infer each new case by minimizing governing-equation, boundary/initial, and data-regularization losses.
Use automatic differentiation so the learned basis remains compatible with PDE residual evaluation on different meshes.
evidence_signal: The paper reports tests on advection-diffusion, Burgers', and nonlinear pendulum problems, with lower solution and parameter errors than vanilla PINNs and online speedups from about 10x to over 1000x.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and representativeness of the offline training ensemble, so poor basis coverage may limit generalization to new regimes.
paper_title: Linearized PINN with pretrained nonlinear layers
